headline: Structure prediction and curated data resources converge on peptide annotation and discovery
label: Computational Peptide Discovery Tools
summary: New peptide-focused resources span a condition-resolved bioactivity database, NRP comparison software, and structure-based fold annotation of a salivary EV protein.
synthesis: The items share a tooling orientation toward peptides and small natural-product-like molecules rather than a single method. DBAASP V4 links peptides and peptidomimetics to condition-resolved antimicrobial, antibiofilm, anticancer and cytotoxicity data, supporting data-driven discovery. Peptorama draws non-ribosomal peptide structures and compares known and BGC-predicted NRPs at the peptide level, with reduced runtimes relative to BGC-level comparison. The leech salivary-EV study uses ESMFold with Foldseek/TM-align to assign a Ly-6/uPAR three-finger fold and flags a structurally dark fraction; it is a single-protein annotation, not a platform. DEEPNET-LLM, which predicts metabolite structures from MS/MS spectra through molecular-neighborhood restriction, is adjacent, addressing small-molecule rather than peptide identification. The common thread is connecting predicted structure, curated bioactivity and genome- or spectrum-derived candidates into usable outputs.
